rationale: Detects and throttles automated abuse traffic while keeping service for normal users, which is resistance to attack.
Requires fingerprint enrolment and matching scan to verify the researcher's identity.
A signature with a private key makes later changes detectable (integrity) and ties the reservation to the signing agency employee (origin); non-repudiation is not mentioned.
Validates a device's signed certificate against a trusted issuer before accepting it, which authenticates the device.
Ending the session and revoking the token limits exposure to someone misusing a lost phone (rule 7).
Requires verifying the identity of every person and app before accepting commands.
Requires identity verification through valid credentials before accepting commands.
Suspending a compromised session and refusing its commands contains an ongoing intrusion.
Re-confirms the clinician's identity with challenge questions before opening a restricted record.
Restricts editing of a configuration to its owner (integrity) and requires successful identity verification (authenticity).
Stores a digest and flags corruption when comparison fails, which detects alteration of records.
Protects the encryption keys of patient files in a hardware vault, safeguarding data from disclosure.
Detects and refuses a resubmitted transaction with a repeated identifier, which is replay protection.
Compares downloads against a published digest and flags altered files, which detects modification.
Regenerates the authentication code covering the cumulative debit total so stored data stays consistent and tamper-evident.
Rejects nodes failing certificate verification (authenticity) and isolates nodes after repeated forged identities (resistance).
Encrypts stored statements so they cannot be read by someone obtaining the media.
A hash over each record lets the terminal detect tampering.
Requires verifying the profile owner (authenticity) before allowing edits to stored entries (restricts modification).
Grants a session only when submitted credentials match a registered account.
Role-based limits on viewing and editing restrict both who can read and who can modify data (rule 3).
Restricts creation, editing and deletion of reference scenarios to one role.
Verifies the service's certificate against its claimed domain, authenticating the service.
Scans plug-ins for malicious code and refuses infected ones, resisting malware.
Requires stored values to match the source and flags checksum mismatches, ensuring data accuracy.
Terminates the session and invalidates the token server-side on close, limiting session abuse (rule 7).
Encrypts client connections so query traffic cannot be read in transit.
Identifies each connection by validating an account name and secret before queries.
Only administrators may change the limit and no other user may view it, restricting both modification and reading.
Restricts who can change modification rights and stores a hash to detect alteration of reservations.
Computes and stores an integrity code over running totals to detect alteration.
Account lockout after repeated failed sign-ins contains brute-force attacks (rule 1); credential verification is not mentioned.
Rejects unprivileged attempts to insert, update or delete protected records, restricting modification.
Only the owner may open, trim or overwrite a capture, restricting both reading and modification.
Changes to rules or firmware require owner approval, restricting unauthorized modification; whether owner identity must be verified is not stated.
A server-issued expiring one-time code is required to complete login, which authenticates the employee.
Reacts to a detected replayed authorisation by halting the payment and ending the session, resisting replay attacks.
Only the build manager may change shared project settings, restricting modification.
Detects and refuses alteration of the stored balance outside validated operations, protecting data integrity.
